To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a core width of ~9 mm in a stabrite-coaked LHC-inner-type 28-strand Rutherford cable is needed to obtain a R⊥, eff of 15 μ Ω, and that this value can be attained without the need for a diffusion heat treatment.
a 28-strand LHC-inner type cable can be cured at 170°C and 80 MPa and that by inserting a 8.5-mm-wide stainless steel core, the effective contact resistance, R⊥,eff, can be reduced to 15 μΩ.

the effective interstrand contact resistance of a stabritecoated Rutherford cable can, by varying the width, be varied over a range of more than 100:1 and that the target ICR of 15 μΩ is attainable with a core width that leaves the rest of the conductor free for current sharing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of the interstrand contact resistivity, R⊥,eff, of a Rutherford-type cable, which has been coated with a thin layer of stabrite, a silver-epoxy composite.
the effect of a stainless steel insert on the interstrand contact resistance (IC) in a Rutherford cable.
a method of controlling the interstrand resistance of stabrite-coated Rutherford cables, and the method is applicable to all cables, including the LHC outer type. Proc. SPIE 5172, Superconduct
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a core width of approximately 8.5-9.5 mm is the best choice for stabrite-coated Rutherford cables.
the ICR of the LHC-inner-type cables is a function of core width and that a core width of about one-half of the cable width is required to obtain the target ICR of 15 μΩ.

by varying the width, w, of a stainless steel (SS) core in the stabrite-coated Rutherford cable the effective interstrand contact resistance can be varied from a value of 1.3 μΩ (no core) up to 15.0 μΩ (w=12.7 mm), and that the OSU-administrated CERN diffusion HT is equivalent to inserting an 8.5-mm-wide SS core.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a stainless steel core of width 8.5-9.5 mm is the most effective means to obtain a satisfactory contact resistance in stabrite-coating-coated Rutherford cable.
the OSU diffusion HT, in the case of the LHC-inner-type cable used in this work, is equivalent to inserting a stainless steel core of width approximately one-half that of the cable.
by using a core width of about 10 mm the ICR of the cable is reduced to the level of 15 μΩ and the cable can be operated at the LHC design field of 8 T with a loss level of 1 W/m.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ICR can be varied in a controlled fashion by varying the core width, and that the core need not occupy the entire cable width.
the width of a steel core in a stabrite-coached Rutherford cable can, by itself, provide a means of controlling the ICR to a desired level.
the effective contact resistance of a stabritecoated LHC-inner type Rutherford cable can readily be adjusted by adjusting the width and/or the composition of a core.
